deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three related pieces of work on binary quadratic forms, in the Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (DA) setting of forms (a,b,c) with determinant D = b^2 - ac. It continues the previous page, which tabulated period sequences for primes 4n+1 and counted them by class number.

(A) Positive determinant 1679 (upper left and upper middle).
- Gauss factors 1679 = 23*73. Above this he writes '3.8.7.11, 13.17.19 [25 struck]'. Its purpose is unclear: possibly a list of moduli for his exclusion method, or a test of 1679 against small moduli. I cannot reconstruct it with certainty.
- He then develops sqrt(1679) by the usual recursion (notation mine): P_{k+1} = a_k Q_k - P_k, Q_{k+1} = (D - P_{k+1}^2)/Q_k, a_k = floor((P_k + sqrt D)/Q_k).
- Principal period, starting P=40, Q=1: 1679 - 40^2 = 79, so Q = 1, 79, 2, 79, 1, ... His column reads +1, -79, +2.
- In this column the numbers (-1)^k Q_k are the values A^2 - D B^2 of the convergents, i.e. numbers represented by the principal form. In the language of forms this is the period of reduced forms (1,40,-79), (-79,39,2), (2,39,-79), ...
- Second period: he starts at a reduced 'P' divisible by 23, namely P=23, Q=23 (23 divides 1679 - 529 = 1150). This gives
  P = 23, 23, 27, 30, 11, 27, 23, 23, ...
  Q = 23, 50, 19, 41, 38, 25, 46, 25, 38, 41, 19, 50, 23.
  The P-values 23, 27, 30 are written beside '4 Ordines'. The marginal 1558 = 1679 - 11^2 = 41*38 is the step giving Q = 38.
  Written with alternating signs: -23, +50, -19, +41, -38, +25, -46.
- The column headed 23 repeats both periods with all signs reversed (-1, +79, -2; +23, -50, ...). That is the opposite cycle.
- Hence '4 Ordines': four cycles (periods), namely the principal one, its negative, the 23-cycle, and its negative.
- Under 73 a further start '+5' is begun but not continued. It would plausibly be the form (5,38,-47), since 38^2 - 1679 = -235 = -5*47.

(B) Negative determinant -6256, with 6256 = 16*17*23 (upper right table and scattered computations).
- A form (a,b,c) here has b^2 - ac = -6256, i.e. ac = b^2 + 6256. The pairs 'a,b' in the table all satisfy a | b^2 + 6256:
  (1,0,6256); (25,12,256) [6400 = 25*256, the '6400 256' written beside 245]; (52,46,161) [8372 = 52*161]; (49,4,128) [6272]; (5,2,1252) [6260, written]; (61,24,112) [6832]; (37,21,181) [6697]; (68,34,109) [7412; the image shows a corrected first number, read as 68].
- Rows 1,3,5,7 are the residue class mod 8 of the numbers represented. The column '—' versus '17.23' records the quadratic characters with respect to 17 and 23: '—' means both residues, '17.23' means both nonresidues. The margin '-23.17' belongs to this.
- Row 1, column '—' (principal genus): 1, 25, 52 (=4*13), 49. Each is a quadratic residue of both 17 and 23.
- Row 5, column '17.23': 5, 61, 37, 109. Each is a nonresidue of both 17 and 23.
- So this is the genus classification (DA arts. 229-233). There are characters mod 4, mod 8, mod 17 and mod 23; the product relation leaves 2^3 = 8 genera = 4 rows x 2 columns. He lists four classes in each of two genera.
- The scattered computations are composition/reduction steps, each of the form b^2 + 6256 = a*c:
  - 6256 + 37^2 = 7625 = 125*61, i.e. (61,37,...) ~ (61,-24).
  - 6256 + 58^2 = 9620 = 260*37, giving (37,58,260) ~ (37,21).
  - 6256 + 98^2 = 15860 = 260*61, again reducing mod 61 to (61,24) up to sign.
  - 6256 + 102^2 = 16660 = 49*340, giving (49,102,340) ~ (49,4,128).
  - 6256 + 53^2 = 9065 = 245*37, giving (37,53,245) ~ (37,16,176) ~ (37,-21).
  - Bottom: (77,60,128) [77*128 = 9856 = 3600 + 6256] and (85,17,77) [6545 = 17^2 + 6256 = 85*77]; 1309 = 6545/5.
- The bottom chain 3,5,13,5,3,3,5,13,..., the fractions 1/10, 3/13, 13/6, 6/15, and the numbers 130 and 390 seem to be another reduction or period computation. Their determinant cannot be identified with confidence.

(C) Continued-fraction periods of sqrt(D) for D = 243, 244, 245, 246.
- Notation: left numbers are (-1)^k Q_k, right numbers are P_k, as in (A).
- 243: Q = 1, 18, 13, 11, 9, 2 and P = 15, 3, 10, 12, 15.
- 244: Q = 1, 19, 12, 15, 13, 16, 9, 20, 5, 15, 16, 3, 25, 4 and P = 15, 4, 8, 7, 6, 10, 8, 12, 13, 2, 14, 13, 12. The listing stops at Q = 4, which is followed by a symmetric reversal.
- 245: Q = 1, 20, 11, 19, 4, 5 and P = 15, 5, 6, 13, 15.
- 246: Q = 1, 21, 10, 5, 25, 2 and P = 15, 6, 14, 11, 14.
- These are half-periods up to the symmetry point. The next page continues the same computations for 247-255.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the continued-fraction columns for 1679, 243, 244, 245 and 246; every Q_{k+1} = (D - P_{k+1}^2)/Q_k checks.

All legible form pairs for determinant -6256 satisfy a | b^2 + 6256. The one doubtful entry, transcribed '58,34', fails (7412/58 is not an integer) but works as 68,34 (7412 = 68*109). It is presumably a corrected or misread numeral, not an error by Gauss.

The note '3.8.7.11, 13.17.19' cannot be verified as any single coherent residue statement: -1679 is a quadratic residue mod 3, 7, 11, 17 and is ≡1 mod 8, but is a nonresidue mod 13 and 19. Its meaning stays unclear.

results.what: Periods of reduced forms / continued fraction of sqrt(D) for D = 1679, including a non-principal cycle through 23; recognition of 4 cycles ('ordines') of forms of determinant 1679
results.modern_name: Cycles of reduced indefinite binary quadratic forms; continued-fraction (PQa) algorithm for quadratic irrationals

results.what: Continued-fraction half-periods of sqrt(243), sqrt(244), sqrt(245), sqrt(246) with the P,Q sequences
results.modern_name: Continued fraction expansion of sqrt(D) / period of the principal form
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange; tabulated by Gauss and others

results.what: Distribution of classes of determinant -6256 = -16*17*23 into genera by characters mod 8, mod 17 and mod 23, with listed classes (1,0,6256), (25,12,256), (52,46,161), (49,4,128) and (5,2,1252), (61,24,112), (37,21,181), (68,34,109)
results.modern_name: Genus theory of binary quadratic forms (assigned characters)

results.what: Reduction of forms obtained in composition, e.g. (49,102,340) to (49,4,128) and (37,58,260) to (37,21,181)
results.modern_name: Gaussian reduction / composition of positive definite forms

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for Gauss's own Disquisitiones theory: periods of indefinite forms, genus characters, and reduction. It belongs to the same series of class-number tabulations as the neighbouring pages. Nothing goes beyond what he published in 1801; the only interest is as a record of his computational practice.

checkable.asserts: listed pairs are forms (a,b,c) of determinant -6256

checkable.sympy: [legendre_symbol(n,17) for n in [25,13,49]] + [legendre_symbol(n,23) for n in [25,13,49]] == [1]*6
checkable.asserts: principal-genus entries 25, 52 (via 13) and 49 are residues of 17 and 23 (legendre_symbol from sympy.ntheory)

checkable.sympy: [legendre_symbol(n,17) for n in [5,61,37,109]] + [legendre_symbol(n,23) for n in [5,61,37,109]] == [-1]*8
checkable.asserts: row-5 entries are nonresidues of both 17 and 23 (column '17.23')

transcription_corrections: The numbers 23, 27, 30 beside '4 Ordines' are the P-values (23, 27, 30) of the second cycle, not a separate column of Q-values.
In the 6256 table the last entry of row 5, transcribed '58,34', is a corrected numeral; arithmetic requires 68,34 (6256 + 34^2 = 7412 = 68*109).
'16.17.23' is written with a mark after 16 ('16'''), probably an emphasis or exponent mark; the product 16*17*23 = 6256 is correct.
'245 6400 256' combines the heading 245 with the separate computation 6256 + 12^2 = 6400 = 25*256 for the form (25,12,256).
The marginal '1558 / 38' belongs to the 1679 cycle: 1679 - 11^2 = 1558 = 41*38.
